# Agent Crew — The Last Spellroad

Course deliverable: **Multi-Agent AI for Game Development, Assignment #3 — Build an Agent Crew.**

## What this is

**Game:** [The Last Spellroad](../docs/game/the-last-spellroad-design.md) — a low-spec, top-down, Tibia-like magical roguelite where a wandering mage fights tile-based enemy waves down an endless road generated by an in-fiction AI Encounter Director.

This is a real, runnable [CrewAI](https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI) program — 8 LLM agents coordinating through an actual task pipeline (`crew/crew.py`, `Process.sequential`), not a diagram of an idea. Given a level number, the crew produces one complete, validated **content bundle** for that level: a new enemy-wave encounter, a new spell tuned to it, an economy validation pass, art-sourcing notes, a lore beat, an engine-integration note, an adversarial critique, and a final ship/block status — all written as real files to `output/run_<timestamp>/`.

The 8 agents are the same roster already designed for this game in `docs/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` — Ana, Warden, Frieren, Pato, Tilesmith, Lorena, Loomwright, Heckler — reimplemented here as executable CrewAI `Agent`/`Task` objects instead of Claude Code sub-agent prompts. See `CONTEXT.md` for exactly how this relates to that existing roster.

## What it produces, concretely

One run produces, for a given level:

| File | Agent | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `01_ana_kickoff_brief.md` | Ana | Scoped brief for the run |
| `02_warden_wave.md` | Warden | One `wave.json`-schema encounter |
| `03_frieren_spell.md` | Frieren | One `spell.json`-schema spell |
| `04_pato_validation.md` | Pato | PASS / flagged-diff against the Mana, Mastery, and Hexcoin templates |
| `05_tilesmith_art_notes.md` | Tilesmith | Sourced-asset + license proposal |
| `06_lorena_lore_beat.md` | Lorena | Short in-world flavor text |
| `07_loomwright_integration_notes.md` | Loomwright | Which real engine files this touches, and how |
| `08_heckler_critique.md` | Heckler | Six-persona adversarial critique |
| `09_ana_status_report.md` | Ana | Final `shipped-and-validated` / `blocked-with-reason` / `in-progress-with-owner` verdict |
| `bundle.json` | — | All of the above, combined |

This is the same wave/spell content format already shipping in `src/data/waves/` and `src/data/spells/spells.json` — the crew's output is a genuine proposal for new game content, not a mocked-up example schema. (Promoting a specific run's output into the shipped game data is a separate, deliberate developer decision — see `CONTEXT.md`, "What belongs here.")

## Why this architecture

See `diagram.md` for the full Mermaid diagram. In short: Ana brackets the run (scopes it, then closes it with a status report built from every other agent's output), Warden and Frieren generate in parallel, Pato validates their numbers (never its own — the generator/validator split from the GDD is preserved exactly), Tilesmith/Lorena/Loomwright each add one more layer against the validated content, and Heckler critiques the whole bundle before Ana closes it out. No agent is decorative: Ana's final task's `context` list names all 8 agents' tasks, so removing any one breaks what Ana can report.

## Running it

No paid API key needed — this crew runs entirely against a local [Ollama](https://ollama.com) server (the `ollama` service in the repo's root `docker-compose.yml`).

```bash
cp agent-crew/.env.example agent-crew/.env   # required even empty -- see CONTEXT.md
docker-compose up -d ollama
docker-compose run --rm agent-crew python main.py 2
```

The trailing `2` is the level number (defaults to `2` if omitted). On first run, `main.py` automatically pulls `llama3.2` (the developer's pick: 3B parameters, the best logic/speed/memory balance for an 8GB-class machine) into the `ollama` container — this takes a few minutes and is cached in a named volume afterward. Output lands in `agent-crew/output/run_<timestamp>/`.

**Resource note:** a 3B model needs real headroom. On this machine, Docker runs via [Colima](https://github.com/abiquo/colima) rather than Docker Desktop; its default 2GB/2-CPU VM OOM-killed the model outright (`llama-server process has terminated: signal: killed`) until bumped to 8GB/4 CPUs (`colima stop && colima start --cpu 4 --memory 8`). If you hit the same error, check your own Docker/Colima/Docker-Desktop memory allocation first.

## Model assignment

Per-agent model choice (`crew/config.py`) mirrors the shape of the living GDD's own Model-Selection Governance table -- one cheaper/faster model for deterministic work, a more capable one for generative/creative work -- but with local Ollama models instead of paid Claude tiers. For now every agent defaults to the same shared model (`llama3.2`) as a same-day-deadline simplification; the config already supports a genuinely different model per agent (e.g. a smaller/faster model for Pato's rule-checking, a larger one for Warden/Frieren's generative work) via per-agent env vars once there's runway to test that a larger model still finishes in reasonable time on CPU. See `.env.example`.

## Known limitations of this run

`output/run_20260728_225706/` is a real, captured run — not curated or cherry-picked. Worth being honest about what a small (3B), CPU-only, zero-cost local model actually produces, since the point of this crew is coordination, not model quality:

- Warden's wave and Frieren's spell drift from the exact `wave.json`/`spell.json` schema in places (e.g. `weight: "Standard"` instead of the lowercase `"standard"` the real data uses, an `hp_modifier`/`damage_modifier` nested inside the enemy entry instead of the wave). Pato's validation pass doesn't reliably catch every one of these -- a real numeric-template check would need either a larger model or a code-level schema validator in front of Pato's task, not just a prompt.
- Heckler's critique came back terse (a cost-benefit JSON blob) rather than the full six distinct persona voices the task asks for -- a known small-model tendency to compress a multi-part instruction into the shortest thing that satisfies it.
- The coordination itself is real, though: Ana's closing status (`09_ana_status_report.md`) is `blocked-with-reason`, and its justification correctly reasons from Heckler's specific negative verdict -- not a templated default. That cross-agent dependency working correctly, on a free local model, is the actual point of this assignment.

Swapping `CREW_DEFAULT_MODEL` (or per-agent overrides) for a larger local model, once one's been confirmed to run in reasonable time, should tighten schema adherence without changing anything about the architecture above.
